advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests exercising rebar._optional.capability_installed and rebar._optional.require_capability (the delegating wrappers), including their lazy-import path.
evidence: search_files for `capability_installed` returns only the definition src/rebar/_optional.py:187 — no test reference
search_files for `require_capability` in tests shows only tests/unit/test_capabilities.py calling `cap.require_capability` (the _capabilities module), never `_optional.require_capability`
The delegators exist specifically to avoid an import cycle via lazy import (`from rebar import _capabilities`); that behavior is untested.
advisory.finding: The new public delegators capability_installed() and require_capability() added to _optional.py have no tests. capability_installed appears in no test file, and _optional.require_capability (whose lazy import-cycle-avoiding delegation is the point of the wrapper) is never invoked by any test — tests only call rebar._capabilities.require_capability directly. A regression in the lazy `from rebar import _capabilities` delegation (e.g. reintroducing the import cycle or mis-delegating the key) would not be caught.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add two tests: assert _optional.capability_installed(key) mirrors _capabilities.is_available(key), and assert _optional.require_capability('audit_ui') raises OptionalDependencyError under block_extra.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the require_capability no-op-when-present test deterministic instead of conditional (swap in an error-posture Capability whose probe is a guaranteed-present stdlib module).
evidence: tests/unit/test_capabilities.py:140 `assert cap.require_capability("agent_runtime") is None` — reached only when the probe happens to be installed
The registry is explicitly meant to run in a leanest no-extras install (module docstring), where this branch never executes.
advisory.finding: test_require_capability_is_noop_when_probe_present guards its only assertion behind `if cap.is_available('agent_runtime')`, so in any environment where the agents extra is absent (the lean/no-extras install the registry is designed for) the test body asserts nothing and passes vacuously — it cannot detect a regression where require_capability wrongly raises for an available error-posture capability.
advisory.suggested_fix: Use dataclasses.replace to build an error-posture Capability with probe='sys' (always importable), register it via validate/get shim or test is_available+require directly on it, so the available branch always executes.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Tighten the is_available isolation assertion to prove non-execution (e.g. assert the probe module object has no executed attributes / use a sys.modules before-after diff) rather than the always-true __spec__ escape hatch.
evidence: tests/unit/test_capabilities.py:167 `assert probe not in sys.modules or getattr(sys.modules.get(probe), "__spec__", None) is not None`
An executed module in sys.modules has __spec__ set, so the second disjunct is satisfied by the very leak (execution) the test claims to forbid.
The stronger test_registry_never_imports_a_probe_package (line 144) uses a before/after sys.modules diff and does verify non-execution; this weaker test adds no real oracle.
advisory.finding: test_is_available_does_not_leave_probe_in_sys_modules asserts `probe not in sys.modules or getattr(sys.modules.get(probe), '__spec__', None) is not None`. A module that was genuinely EXECUTED (imported) also has a non-None __spec__, so the OR right-hand branch passes even on a real import leak — the assertion cannot distinguish 'spec cached without execution' from 'module fully imported', defeating its stated isolation oracle.
advisory.suggested_fix: Assert `probe not in sys.modules` directly (find_spec does not insert into sys.modules for a not-yet-imported module), or record sys.modules before the call and assert the probe was not added.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a boundary test that blocks the pydantic_ai bedrock provider import and asserts build_bedrock_provider raises LLMConfigError containing `pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]`.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:127-129 raises LLMConfigError with `install_hint('bedrock_provider')` when `from pydantic_ai.providers.bedrock import BedrockProvider` fails
test_capabilities.py:114 asserts install_hint at the registry level but never through the bedrock boundary
By contrast test_audit_serve_heldout.py:117 asserts `nava-rebar[ui]` at the serve boundary and test_jira_dc_transport.py:194 asserts the jira-datacenter install string at the transport boundary
search_files for `optional bedrock provider` finds only the source line 128 — no test blocks the BedrockProvider import to assert the message.
advisory.finding: The bedrock provider missing-package boundary (bedrock_model.py:118-129), rewired in this diff to source its install string from install_hint('bedrock_provider'), has no test that drives the ImportError branch and asserts the resulting LLMConfigError message. The sibling boundaries changed in the same diff (audit serve, jira transport) each retain a boundary test asserting their install string; this one does not, so a regression in the bedrock branch's message would go uncaught.
advisory.suggested_fix: Use block_extra (or monkeypatch sys.modules) to make `from pydantic_ai.providers.bedrock import BedrockProvider` raise ImportError, then assert build_bedrock_provider(cfg) raises LLMConfigError whose message contains the registry install hint.
